name: Egyptian Nile sailboat model
description: A Middle Kingdom Egyptian model depicts the intended use of a sail for river travel.

places.note: Present-day country or region reference; ancient political boundaries are not implied.

date.label: ca. 1981–1975 BCE
date.basis: Museum gives an approximate date for the model; no first invention date is implied.

events.statement: A model from Meketre’s tomb depicts a riverboat preparing to sail on its return journey.
events.caveats: This is a ritual representation; the sail itself is missing and a particular real-life voyage is not established.

evidence.supports: The Met dates the model and interprets the missing sail being raised.
Museum interprets the paired models as a northbound paddling and return sailing funerary pilgrimage.

events.scope: A funerary model interpreted as the sailing return leg of a pilgrimage to Abydos.

caveats: Earlier sailing evidence may exist; this ritual model witnesses representation rather than the first voyage or a direct technical genealogy.
